output.reason: A 68-year-old with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle swelling plus new orthopnea forcing him to sit up to breathe for two nights suggests decompensating heart failure needing immediate emergency assessment with oxygen saturation, imaging and blood tests.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Worsening swelling in both ankles plus needing to sit up to breathe at night can mean fluid backing up from your heart or lungs, and that needs same-hour oxygen checks, a chest image and blood tests. Have someone drive you, or call 911 if breathing becomes harder, you feel chest pain, or you faint.
differential: Decompensated heart failure with pulmonary congestion
Other cause of fluid overload (kidney or liver disease)
